amnesty

AM-nes-tee — contains 'amnesia,' forgetting; an amnesty officially 'forgets' past offenses. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Amnesty is an official pardon granted to people who have committed an offense.

The city offered a brief amnesty on overdue library fines, letting patrons return books without paying a cent.

Worked Example

A country ends a long civil war and announces that any soldier who lays down their weapon within one month will not be prosecuted for fighting, no matter which side they fought on.

Officially agreeing not to punish people for past offenses is exactly what an amnesty is. Unlike 'apology,' which is just an expression of regret, amnesty is a formal, official pardon.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

pardon: A pardon is official forgiveness for an offense, and it is usually granted to one named person whose case is weighed individually. An amnesty works at a different scale: one blanket decision that pardons a whole group or an entire category of offenses at once.

reprieve: A reprieve cancels or postpones a punishment: the penalty is lifted or delayed, but the offense itself stays on the books. An amnesty reaches further, officially forgiving the offense itself so that no punishment can ever attach to it again.

forgiveness: Forgiveness is the personal act of no longer holding an offense against someone, and anyone who was wronged can offer it. An amnesty is never personal: it is an official, government-level pardon that erases a whole category of offenses.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

prosecution: the act of taking legal action against someone

punishment: a penalty imposed for an offense

Where it sits · how far protection from punishment reaches — leniency → amnesty → immunity

leniency vs. amnesty: Leniency is weaker than amnesty — leniency just means a lighter punishment, while amnesty means the offense is officially forgiven entirely, with no punishment at all.

immunity vs. amnesty: Immunity can be stronger than amnesty: amnesty forgives a past offense, but immunity protects someone from prosecution for actions taken even in the future.

The pieces

prefix — a-

prefix — a-: without, not (Greek)

root — -mnes-: memory (Greek)

suffix — -ty

suffix — -ty: state of (English)

Put it together

Put it together: Greek amnestia combined a- (without) with mnesis (memory) — literally 'forgetting.' An amnesty is an official decision to 'forget' past offenses rather than punish them.
